MyLife
@Persistent
At Persistent, well-being is not a benefit, it is a belief. Created by Dr. Anand Deshpande,
MyLife@Persistent continues to be the cultural and structural backbone of how we care for our
people. In FY26, the framework evolved from a wellness programme to a holistic charter, to help
employees and their families lead healthier, more connected and more fulfilling lives.
Rooted in our philosophy of work-life harmony, MyLife@Persistent operates across the four
dimensions of Physical, Emotional, Social and Financial Wellness, delivered through the eight
structured offerings of Awareness & Education, Workshops, Communities, Transformation
Programmes, Personalised Counselling, Flagship Events, Unwind & Energisers and Team Bonding.
In FY26, we deepened personalisation further through our N=1 approach, scaled the wellness
ambassadors programme across global locations and introduced gamified digital challenges that
made everyday well-being more engaging.
The result: a vibrant ecosystem where every employee feels seen, supported and celebrated.

At Persistent Foundation, we believe meaningful progress is created when
innovation, inclusion and collective action come together with a purpose.
As technology reshapes industries and societies at unprecedented speed,
we believe it must also expand opportunity, strengthen resilience and contribute
meaningfully to the communities and ecosystems that sustain long-term progress.
For more than 17 years, the Foundation has worked alongside marginalised and
underprivileged communities, institutions and grassroots partners to help create
opportunities that endure beyond individual interventions. Whether through
education, healthcare, environmental stewardship or livelihood creation, our focus
remains on enabling long-term capability, dignity and self-reliance. Increasingly,
we see this work not only as social responsibility, but as part of building a more
inclusive and resilient future in which progress is shared more widely and sustainably.
In FY26, Persistent Foundation continued to scale both the reach and depth of its
impact, delivering 65 projects across Education, Health, Community Development
and the Preservation of Heritage and Wildlife. Together, these initiatives touched
the lives of 70,000 individuals and 600 families. We also enabled the plantation of
42,000 trees, reflecting our continued commitment to ecological stewardship and
climate resilience.
What distinguishes the Foundation’s approach is not only the scale of programmes
delivered, but the ecosystems we help strengthen through long-term partnerships,
employee participation and community-led action. Across every initiative, our
objective is to move beyond short-term intervention towards enabling durable
capability and opportunity that can sustain and compound over time.

Report of the Directors
Your Directors are pleased to present the Thirty-sixth Annual Report of your Company along with the Audited
Financial Statements for the Financial Year ended March 31, 2026.
A. Business Update
The theme of this year’s report, Re(AI)magining the Enterprise, reflects both the moment our industry has reached
and the role your Company has chosen within it. Across the world, enterprises are rethinking how they operate,
transform, and compete in the presence of Artificial Intelligence. Ambition is everywhere; what remains scarce is the
engineering execution to turn that ambition into something impactful, governed, and measurable. That intersection,
where AI ambition meets engineering execution, is where your Company does its most consequential work.
It is also where Persistent has always operated. For thirty-six years, your Company has been built not around any
single technology wave but around a more enduring belief that a company stays valuable by continuing to learn,
adapt, and earn its customers’ trust through every cycle of change. AI is the latest and most far-reaching of those
cycles, and one that rewards precisely the strengths your Company has spent decades cultivating, which include
engineering judgement, technical depth, and the discipline to execute responsibly at scale.
Your Company entered this moment having built capability ahead of demand, and Financial Year 2025-26 reflected
the payoff. In Financial Year 2025-26, Revenue was US$ 1,654.4 Million, growing 17.4% Year-on-Year in US$ terms
and 23.5% in Indian Rupee terms, strengthening your Company’s standing among the fastest-growing companies
in the industry. Q4FY 26 marked the 24th consecutive quarter of sequential growth; a cadence achieved by only a
handful of companies. Profitability strengthened even as the Company continued to invest ahead of demand, full-year
EBIT margin expanded to 15.6%, and Profit After Tax rose 33% to INR 18,651 Million, with the fourth-quarter EBIT
margin reaching 16.3%. On the strength of this performance, the Board recommended a final dividend of INR 18 per
share, bringing the total dividend for the year to INR 40 per share, up from INR 35 per share a year earlier, subject to
shareowners’ approval. As AI adoption accelerated, your Company’s AI-led, platform-driven approach strengthened
its operating model from within, improving the quality, velocity, and scale of everything it delivers. The defining lesson
of the year, visible across every industry, is that success with AI depends less on the sophistication of any single model
than on operational maturity, including clean, well-governed data, redesigned processes, an enabled workforce, and
responsible governance. Enterprises are no longer seeking a vendor of AI features; they are seeking a partner who can
make AI work safely, repeatably, and accountably, inside the systems on which their business already runs. That is the
role your Company has built itself to play: through a model that is platform-centric, IP-led, and outcome-based, and in
which it is consistently its own first customer.
Across its three industry verticals, Software, Hi-Tech and Emerging Industries; Banking, Financial Services and
Insurance; and Healthcare and Life Sciences, this strategy is advancing on several reinforcing fronts:
• Engineering Hyper Productivity. Your Company’s Generative AI-enabled engineering platform, SASVA, reached
its fourth generation, with SASVA 4.0 becoming generally available in April 2026 and backed by a portfolio of
more than 120 patents. Shifting the focus from individual productivity to team intelligence, its “Brain” holds the
full organisational context and validates workflows by simulation before execution, while integration with partner
models, frontier models such as Anthropic’s Claude and OpenAI’s GPT, lets clients bring their own model of
choice and tooling into a single, governed environment that accelerates software development and reduces
technical debt at scale.
• Business Hyper Productivity. Your Company is reimagining end-to-end business workflows as self-orchestrating
ecosystems of AI agents. During the year it enhanced its GenAI Hub and Agent Studio, launched an Agent
Processing Unit to onboard and orchestrate external agents, and grew its portfolio to more than 250 enterprise
agents with deep domain coverage across BFSI and Healthcare and Life Sciences.
• Enterprise Data Readiness. Trusted, contextual and governed data is the foundation of scaled enterprise AI
readiness and adoption. To accelerate this journey, your Company enhanced its iAURA platform with a modern
interface, agentified Data Engineering Lifecycle, and an AI Data Mapper and Modeller grounded in a semantic
layer. A new Enterprise Data Assessment capability builds knowledge graphs and enterprise data context,
capturing business meaning, relationships, and domain knowledge, giving AI agents the memory to act with
precision. A Cost of Intelligence capability brings governance, making AI spend measurable and accountable,
giving enterprises the trusted foundations on which durable AI value is built.

Report of the Directors
• C ustomer Zero. Your Company is its own first customer, deploying its modular Agentic AI platform, AssistX,
across its internal functions to compress incident-resolution times and automate large parts of its operations,
moving from systems of record to systems of action. Every capability therefore reaches clients already proven in
production, and the experience continually sharpens the Company’s offerings.
• Non-linear, platform-led economics. Platform-driven pricing is contributing a meaningful margin tailwind, as
your Company progressively shifts its revenue mix towards non-linear engagements in which value is increasingly
decoupled from headcount.
• Vertical depth. Representative engagements during the year included a large-scale shift from hardware-centric
products to software-led platforms for a global industrial technology leader, the modernisation of a payments
platform for one of the largest banks in the Nordics, the co-building of a fully digital underwriting platform for one
of Australia’s largest life insurers, and the reimagining of a global Contract Research Organisation platform into a
single, cloud-first architecture for a global life sciences leader.
Underpinning these engagements is your Company’s 3C Framework, Core, Context, and Coordination.
This architecture enables enterprises to move AI from fragmented pilots to integrated, enterprise-wide results.
Core provides the governed, cloud-agnostic foundation that secures, observes, and cost-controls every AI workload
from day one.
Context supplies the enterprise intelligence, grounding agents in verified data, knowledge graphs, institutional
memory, and domain semantics so that they speak the language of the business.
Coordination orchestrates auditable, multi-agent workflows across functions and systems of record, enabling people
and agents to collaborate at production scale with full traceability. Each pillar reinforces the others, and together
they turn isolated AI experiments into outcomes the business can trust and repeat — the foundation on which your
Company is building durable, AI-led transformation for its clients.
Your Company continued to widen the ecosystem through which it builds the next generation of solutions. During the
year, NVIDIA elevated your company to its Advanced Technology Partner program and partnered on a drug-discovery
accelerator; AWS enhanced your company’s partnership status to Strategic Global Systems Integrator; Microsoft
awarded the final designations needed to complete all six Solution Partner Designations; and ServiceNow elevated
your company to Premier partner. Your Company also deepened its partnerships and innovations with Databricks
and Snowflake, advanced model-development collaborations with Anthropic and OpenAI, and announced a new
partnership with Lyzr AI for enterprise process modernisation. Your Company also deepened its collaboration with
academia, co-developing the AI Value Compass with IIM Ahmedabad, a research-based framework for prioritising
and scaling enterprise AI investments. This partnership is part of a broader commitment to co-innovate with leading
institutions and help elevate the country’s AI talent landscape.
To enable and empower every team member of your Company across 21 countries, along this AI transformation
journey, your Company convened AI Huddle in Pune for more than 1700 senior leaders and engineers and, through
Persistent University and a company-wide AI fluency program, completed over 32,500 internal and 6,000 external AI
certifications during the year.
Your Company’s momentum was widely recognised worldwide. It was named the fastest-growing IT services brand
globally in the 2026 Brand Finance IT Services 25 Report, ranked among Asia-Pacific’s top 10 Professional Services
Companies in the TIME 2026 list, and positioned as a Leader in both the Everest Group Software Product Engineering
and Private Equity Services PEAK Matrix® Assessments 2026. It was named a Strong Performer in the Gartner Voice
of the Customer for Public Cloud IT Transformation Services 2026, and its talent and people practices were honoured
at the ET Human Capital Awards, the InfiniT Awards, and by the Confederation of Indian Industry.
Your Company’s commitment to responsible business deepened further. Its sustainability performance earned best-
in-class ratings, including continued recognition in the Dow Jones Sustainability Indices and an S&P Global Corporate
Sustainability Assessment score of 86. Your Company also continued to make progress on renewable energy across
its owned campuses and to scale community and life-saving initiatives through the Persistent Foundation across India
and the United States. Through it all, your Company holds to a human-centred view of this technology: AI does not
replace people; it enables them to do far more, far faster, and judgment, creativity, and integrity will matter more, not
less, in the years ahead.

Future Outlook
In FY 2025-26, your Company’s strategy moved from foundational frameworks to platform-led execution and
into operating models that clients now adopt at scale. As it enters FY 2026-27, its priorities are clear: to deepen AI
adoption, advance the Core, Context, and Coordination foundation, scale its largest client relationships, expand
across geographies, and convert AI investment into measurable business outcomes, while progressively shifting its
revenue mix towards non-linear, platform-led engagements. Built on thirty-six years of engineering depth, governed
data, client trust, and execution discipline, your Company is positioned to capture a market opportunity larger
than any it has faced before and remains firmly on track towards its aspiration of a US$ 2 billion revenue run-rate in
FY 2026-27, continuing to do what it has always done best: turning the enterprise’s AI ambition into engineering
execution that endures.

Policy for the appointment of a new director on the Board
The Board of Directors decides the criteria for the appointment of a new director on the Board from time to time
depending on the dates of retirement of existing Directors and the strategic needs of your Company. The criteria
include expertise area, industry experience, professional background, association with other companies, and similar
important parameters.
Once the criteria are determined, the Board directs the NRC to compile profiles of suitable candidates through
networking, industry associations and business connections. The NRC considers these profiles on the decided
parameters and shortlists the candidates.
For every new member to be added, at least three members of the NRC interact with the panel of candidates.
The panel consists of at least two to four potential candidates.
Efforts are made to ensure that the Board has adequate diversity across various parameters such as nationality,
expertise and gender in terms of the Board Diversity Policy. The Board has decided that for every position of the
Board, at least one female candidate will be part of the shortlisted panel of candidates for consideration.
The Board Diversity Policy adopted by the Board sets out its approach to diversity. The policy is available on the
Company’s website, at https://www.persistent.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/Board-Diversity-Policy.pdf

Your Company is committed to making a difference to the community that we are all part of. Your Company treats the

to improved productivity.

Conservation.

in socially relevant causes. With the cooperation of the employees of your Company, the Foundations have
set up several well-defined programmes and activities for the promotion of Health, Education, Community

ESG at Persistent
At Persistent Systems, Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) considerations are embedded in the Company’s
approach to sustainable and responsible value creation. ESG is integrated into company’s core business practices
through a structured governance framework that ensures accountability, risk oversight, and alignment with strategic
priorities and stakeholder expectations.
ESG Governance Framework
The ESG governance model is built on a multi-tiered structure comprising Board oversight, executive accountability,
and a cross-functional ESG Council. This enables effective integration of ESG considerations across business functions
and supports continuous progress against defined objectives.
Stakeholders’ Relationship and ESG Committee: The Stakeholders’ Relationship and ESG Committee at the Board
level assists the Board in overseeing ESG implementation and performance. The Committee convenes biannually to
review progress against ESG priorities, including climate-related risks and emerging focus areas.
Executive Ownership: Responsibility for execution rests with the leadership team:
• The Chief Financial Officer (CFO) and Head – ESG are accountable for driving ESG strategy implementation,
including target setting and resource allocation.
• The Head – ESG works in close coordination with senior management across functions to embed ESG principles
into business operations and decision-making processes.
ESG Vision Statement
• Reduce GHG emissions using technology solutions
• Nurture diverse talent and foster local communities
• Create value for stakeholder by integrating ESG with our business
Embedding ESG into our Business
As part of our ongoing ESG journey, we aim to leverage engineering excellence and digital capabilities to address
global challenges, contribute to a low-carbon future, and support the well-being of our employees, clients, partners,
and communities. We recognise that sustainability is a continuous and evolving process, and we remain focused
on making consistent, measurable progress towards our ESG ambitions while upholding the highest standards of
governance and accountability.
Since 2022, the Company has been a signatory to the United Nations Global Compact (UNGC) and aligns its
practices with the Ten Principles covering human rights, labour, environment, and anti-corruption. These principles
are embedded across the Company’s culture and day-to-day operations.

15H. Now, both types of taxpayers, i.e., those below the age of 60 and those aged 60 and above, will use Form No. 121 to
submit a declaration to avoid relevant income from being subjected to TDS.

form and has replaced earlier Form 10F. It must be filed when a non-resident wants to claim relief under a Double Taxation
Avoidance Agreement (DTAA) as provided in Section 159 of the Income Tax Act, 1961 as amended from time to time.

1. A brief outline of the Company’s CSR policy, including an overview of the projects or programmes proposed to
be undertaken and a reference to the web link to the CSR policy and projects or programmes
The Board of Directors of your Company has developed a Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) Policy to serve as
a framework for guiding the Company’s CSR initiatives. This policy is publicly accessible and can be viewed on the
Company’s official website at CSR Policy.pdf
The CSR Policy outlines the belief that as a responsible Company, employing a large number of employees,
it is the Company’s obligation to contribute to society and the community. The Company has held this belief
since inception. The journey began in 1995 when the Board decided to commit 1% of profits for social causes.
The allocation was subsequently increased to 2% following the introduction of the CSR provisions under the
Companies Act, 2013.
While there are many projects that need CSR support, a more impactful contribution can be achieved by focusing
on specific areas. Accordingly, your Company has decided to focus CSR activities, in four areas:
1. Health,
2. Education,
3. Community Development, and
4. Wildlife and Heritage Conservation
Your Company started the CSR journey in 1995, and the Company formalised its CSR efforts by establishing
a Public Charitable Trust, Persistent Foundation, during the Financial Year 2008-09. In line with the evolving
regulatory framework and to further strengthen governance and execution of CSR activities, the Company
incorporated Persistent India Foundation, a Section 8 Company under the Companies Act, 2013, on May 1, 2024.
During the year under Report, the CSR projects of the Company were implemented through Persistent India
Foundation (the ‘Foundation’) and few other eligible partnering Non-Government Organisations (NGO).
Further, as part of its efforts to extend its CSR approach to geographies, your Company established Persistent
Systems Foundation Inc., a 501(c) no-profit corporation in the United States, during the FY 2022-23. The US
Foundation received the requisite tax exemption approvals during the FY 2024-25. During the FY 2025-26,
the Company undertook CSR initiatives through the US Foundation, aligned with its CSR philosophy of
contributing to the communities it serves and its commitment to undertake socially responsible activities in a
structured manner beyond statutory requirements.
In addition to the impact of the project funded, the Foundation considers the extent to which Persistent’s
employees can contribute to socially relevant projects. Persistent believes in the culture of giving and contributing
and all employees are encouraged to participate in CSR activities of the Foundation.

Education is the cornerstone of societal progress, acting as the primary driver of economic growth, poverty
reduction, and social mobility. Naturally, education remains a cornerstone of the Foundation’s commitment to
building inclusive and sustainable community. The Foundation’s education initiatives focus on supporting students
from underserved communities at different stages of their learning journey - ranging from school education to
higher education and preparation for employment. In addition to academic support, the Foundation follows
a holistic approach that combines academics with sports, digital learning, life skills, and career preparedness,
helping students build confidence, practical abilities, and long-term career readiness.

18 study centres, the Foundation supported 48 schools and four colleges. These initiatives reached

of impactful, scalable, and sustainable education programmes, strengthening access to quality education in the

Health — Helping our littlest fighters win their biggest battles
The Foundation’s health initiatives are driven by a strong commitment to providing accessible, affordable, and
preventive healthcare to underserved communities. The focus is on improving health outcomes by addressing both
immediate medical needs and long-term well-being. The Foundation supports preventive care, treatment-based
assistance, community outreach programmes, and specialised medical interventions to ensure timely and effective
healthcare support for vulnerable populations.
Working closely with credible healthcare institutions and non-governmental organisations, the Foundation
emphasises early diagnosis, timely treatment, and outreach to communities with limited access to quality healthcare
services. Preventive healthcare remains a key priority, helping reduce disease burden and enabling early identification
of health conditions. In addition, the Foundation provides support for specialised and high-cost medical procedures,
ensuring that financial limitations do not prevent individuals from receiving essential treatment.
Key health interventions during the year included:
• Cochlear implant support for children with hearing impairment
• Cardiac surgeries for patients from economically disadvantaged backgrounds
• Support for essential and critical surgeries across multiple medical specialties
These interventions have played a vital role in saving lives and significantly improving the long-term quality of life for
beneficiaries.

Community Development – Livelihood Project
Wildlife and Heritage conservation — Rooting advancement in our cultural and natural inheritance
As part of its commitment to protecting wildlife and maintaining ecological balance, the Foundation supported
the use of technology to strengthen conservation efforts and reduce conflict between humans and wildlife. Drone
cameras were deployed to track the movement of wild animals and monitor forest areas. These drones were also used
for tiger census activities and to observe elephant movement in sensitive corridors. This enabled timely monitoring,
better coordination on the ground, and quicker response to potential risks.
These efforts support the forest department in safeguarding wildlife habitats and help create awareness among local
communities. By providing early alerts and reliable tracking information, the initiatives play an important role in preventing
human-wildlife conflict and improving safety for both people and animals.
Alongside wildlife conservation, the Foundation also supported heritage preservation and public education by contributing to
the upkeep and improvement of museum infrastructure. This included maintenance work and upgrades to essential facilities,
enabling effective use of audio guide systems for visitors.
Infrastructure support was also extended to Shivsrushti, a historic theme park in Pune, where digital display screens were
installed to enhance storytelling and provide visitors with a more engaging and educational experience through immersive
visual content.
In line with its CSR commitment to wildlife care, the Foundation also supported the operations of an aviary providing medical
treatment to injured and rescued birds. During the year, 673 birds across six species received care, of which 509 were
successfully rehabilitated and released back into their natural habitats. These efforts contributed meaningfully to biodiversity
conservation and the restoration of local ecosystems.

Employee Engagement
At the Foundation, employee engagement is at the heart of its CSR efforts, reflecting a culture where employees
voluntarily contribute their time, skills, and care to support communities. Through well-structured volunteering
opportunities across education, health, environment, and community development, employees are encouraged to
participate actively and create meaningful social impact.
During the year, employee volunteering continued to see strong participation. A total of 5,841 employees contributed
11,683 hours across 70 initiatives. Overall, 299 volunteering activities were conducted across 15 locations, reflecting
broad participation and geographic reach.
Volunteering programmes were designed to be inclusive and flexible, enabling employees across roles and locations
to participate alongside their regular work commitments. On average, each volunteer contributed close to two hours,
reflecting consistent and high quality engagement. Locations such as Pune, Nagpur, Hyderabad, and Goa recorded
particularly strong participation, supported by effective local coordination and employee-led initiatives.
In addition to volunteering, employees actively supported the Foundation through donation drives, further
strengthening the culture of giving. Employee contributions during the year amounted to INR 47.12 lakh,
supplemented by INR 34.79 lakh from other sources. Together, these contributions played an important role in
strengthening the Foundation’s social programmes and extending their reach.

Annexure E - Energy Conservation and Technology Absorption: Key Initiatives
The Company has achieved carbon neutrality for Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions for three consecutive years (FY 24, FY
25 and FY 26), as per ISO 14068-1:2023, reflecting its continued focus on climate action and responsible operations.
Carbon neutrality has been sustained through a combination of energy efficiency improvements, increased renewable
energy adoption, and implementation of climate-conscious policies across operations and the value chain. The Company
continues to align its approach with evolving global and national sustainability standards, with a focus on enhancing long-
term environmental resilience.
The Company continues to enhance energy efficiency across its operations through a combination of green building
design, technology adoption, and operational optimisation.
Key energy initiatives include:
Deployment of advanced HVAC solutions:
• Replacement of legacy systems with energy-efficient inverter-based systems using eco-friendly refrigerants (R32 /
R410A)
• Implementation of demand-controlled ventilation systems to optimise energy use and enhance indoor air quality,
reducing treated fresh air AHU power consumption
• Deployment of cold aisle containment in data centres to reduce HVAC energy load
• Installation of HVLS fans in large spaces to enhance comfort and reduce dependence on air conditioning
• Introduction of mist cooling systems in outdoor cafeterias and common areas
• Evaluation and adoption of adiabatic cooling solutions for 24×7 data centre and server room operations
• Automation of AHU for energy saving and human comfort
Lighting Optimisation Initiatives
• Complete transition to LED-based lighting infrastructure
• Adoption of automated, sensor-driven lighting systems, including occupancy and motion sensors, for efficient energy
utilisation
Integrated Energy Management and Operational Efficiency
• Enabled centralised monitoring through an integrated Building Management System (BMS)
• Implemented dynamic optimisation of air conditioning operations, based on occupancy, seasonal variations and work
schedules
• Incorporated energy-efficient design features such as double wall construction, low-E glazing, double-glazed units
(DGUs), underdeck insulation, and optimised daylight utilisation
• Deployed power quality systems (ASVG, AHF, APFC) to maintain near-unity power factor and control harmonics
• Upgraded to high-efficiency modular UPS systems to minimise transmission and operational losses
• Transitioned to a 100% laptop-based computing environment to reduce energy demand and associated HVAC load
• Optimised operations through regulated scheduling of utilities including lifts, lighting, ventilation, water coolers, and
vending machines during non-operating hours
• Installed Variable Frequency Drives (VFDs) in AHUs and fresh air systems for enhanced control and energy optimisation

Report on Corporate Governance
Company’s beliefs on Corporate Governance
“Corporate governance is concerned with holding the balance between economic and social goals and aligning the
interests of individuals, corporations and society.”
- Sir Adrian Cadbury
Redefining Stakeholders for a Sustainable Future
Traditionally, the stakeholders of a public limited company have been defined in legal terms, comprising shareholders,
debenture-holders, deposit-holders, and other security holders. While such a definition remains relevant, the
Company believes that in the context of a modern and evolving business environment, the scope of stakeholders
must extend far beyond statutory classifications.
At Persistent, we recognise that long-term value creation is intrinsically linked with the interests of all those
who contribute to, and are impacted by, our operations. Accordingly, our approach to stakeholder engagement
encompasses not only our investors, but also our employees and their families, customers, business partners, vendors,
regulators, and the communities and ecosystems within which we operate.
In line with this philosophy, the Board of Directors has affirmed a broader and more inclusive definition of
stakeholders. This approach aligns with the Company’s sustainability vision and reinforces its commitment to creating
shared and enduring value for all stakeholder groups.
Our Commitment to Responsible Governance
Corporate Governance is a fundamental cornerstone of our operations and is anchored in the principles of trust,
transparency, and accountability. Our governance framework is designed to balance the interests of a diverse
stakeholder base while enabling robust and ethical decision-making that supports sustainable business growth.
Integrity, inclusivity, and sustainability are fundamental to the Company’s corporate culture. Through continuous
enhancement of governance practices, we strive to uphold the highest standards of accountability while contributing
positively to the broader economic, social, and environmental ecosystem.
This section presents an overview of how the Company engages with stakeholders, integrates Environmental, Social,
and Governance (ESG) considerations into strategy, and seeks to deliver long-term sustainable value.
1. Employees and their Families
The Company’s continued success is driven by the expertise, commitment, and dedication of employees.
Senior employees play a critical role in shaping the Company’s strategic direction and overseeing operations.
Recognising the vital support extended by employees’ families, the Company remains committed to safeguarding
their overall well-being.
2. Clients
The Company provides services to its clients because of which we earn our revenue. Their satisfaction and delight
are important focus areas of the Company’s operations. Our clients are keen that we succeed and continue to
deliver on our promises and hence, they are also vested in our success.
3. Partners
The Company collaborates with its partners to deliver value to its clients. These relationships are built on mutual
trust and shared objectives. The Company believes that the strength and success of its partnerships are integral to
its own growth and endeavours to support the long-term success of its partners.
4. Suppliers
The Company relies on a network of suppliers for various goods and services essential to its operations. Operational
efficiency is closely linked to the quality and reliability of these contributions. The Company is committed to
maintaining fair and sustainable relationships with its suppliers and supporting their long-term growth.

5. Shareowners/Investors
Shareowners are the owners of the Company and are the traditional stakeholders in the Company. They have
invested in the Company, and we believe it is our responsibility to deliver fair returns to our shareowners.
6. Environment
I t is a constant endeavour of the Company to conserve and preserve the environment. Over the years, the Company
has focused on sustainable business practices encompassing economic, environmental, and social imperatives. The
Company also works through Persistent Foundation and Persistent India Foundation, to support projects in the areas of
environmental sustainability and ecological balance.
To maintain and strengthen relationships with its stakeholders, the Company has established structured
mechanisms and governance processes. The Company remains aligned with global sustainability goals and
continues to monitor and enhance its performance against ESG metrics.
Stakeholder relationships are managed through clearly defined roles and responsibilities across the organisation.
The Board of Directors and leadership teams periodically review these activities to ensure adherence to the highest
standards of governance.
T he Nomination and Remuneration Committee (‘NRC’) oversees matters relating to employees, while the Stakeholders’
Relationship and ESG Committee (‘SRC’) is entrusted with addressing the interests of investors, shareholders, and
other security holders in accordance with applicable laws. The Company has also brought ESG oversight within the
purview of the SRC to ensure focused Board-level attention to sustainability initiatives.
T o enable a coordinated approach to stakeholder engagement, the SRC receives inputs from management and other
relevant committees and prepares an annual report for submission to the Board. This report forms an integral part of
the Company’s disclosures.
T he Company believes that strong Corporate Governance practices are essential for enhancing long-term stakeholder
value. Continuous improvement in governance standards remains a key priority, enabling the Company to build trust,
strengthen resilience, and support sustainable growth.
T his Report on Corporate Governance reflects the Company’s ongoing commitment to adhering to governance
principles in both letter and spirit, while striving to maintain the highest standards of integrity and transparency.

included in the agenda. In addition, they have the right to bring matters for discussion at the meeting with the

f. Performance Evaluation of the Board, its Committees and Individual Directors
T he Company conducted the annual performance evaluation of the Board, the Chairman, its various
Committees and the Directors individually, including the Independent Directors. In accordance with the
provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 and the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements)
Regulations, 2015, the performance evaluation was undertaken with the assistance of an external management
consultant specialising in Board evaluations.
The evaluation was carried out through a structured process covering various aspects of the Board’s
functioning, including composition and structure, effectiveness of Board processes, quality and timeliness of
information flow, engagement and participation in deliberations, strategic oversight, governance effectiveness,
risk management and compliance, along with qualitative inputs and perspectives on the future direction of
the Board and the Company. The performance of the Board was assessed through inputs obtained from all
Directors and select senior management executives.
The evaluation process also covered the performance of the Board Committees against the requirements of
their respective charters and the effectiveness in discharging their responsibilities. The external consultant
conducted one-on-one interactions with each Board Member to obtain detailed feedback.
T he Board reviewed and discussed the outcomes of the evaluation in an executive session and noted that
the Board, its Committees and the Directors, including the Independent Directors, continued to function
effectively and demonstrated a high level of engagement, objectivity and preparedness in their roles. The
evaluation process also enabled identification of areas for continuous improvement further improving overall
Board effectiveness. The Board has taken note of these inputs and will address them as part of its ongoing
governance and development initiatives.
The evaluation for FY 2025-26 was conducted in March and April 2026. The findings of the evaluation were
presented at the meetings of the Nomination and Remuneration Committee and the Board of Directors held in
April 2026.

Disclosures
Code of Conduct
Pursuant to the requirements of Regulation 17(5)(a) of Listing Regulations, the Company obtains the affirmation of compliance
of the Code of Conduct from its Directors and Senior Management on a yearly basis since Financial Year 2005-06.
Furthermore, the Code of Conduct applies to all the Company employees and its subsidiaries.
The Code of Conduct is an annual declaration that helps remind all employees and stakeholders the importance of maintaining
the highest standards of ethical business conduct for the Company. In terms of the Code of Conduct, Directors and Employees
must act within the guidelines of the authority conferred upon them and with a duty to make and enact informed decisions and
policies in the best interests of the Company and its shareholders and stakeholders.
Further, Directors and Employees must ensure that they do not derive any undue personal benefit due to their position in the
Company and from the access they have to certain confidential information coming to their knowledge.
It has been affirmed by the Board of Directors that the Code of Conduct has been complied with by all the Board members and
all the Employees and a declaration to this effect forms part of this Report. The Code of Conduct is uploaded on the website of
the Company at Code of Conduct for Directors and Employees | Persistent Systems
In addition to the annual Code of Conduct, the Board has also established a robust Code of Conduct on Prevention of Insider
Trading in terms of the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015. The Company has a zero tolerance policy towards
insider trading, corruption, bribery, and money laundering.
Familiarisation Program for the Board of Directors
Pursuant to the requirements of Regulation 25(7) of Listing Regulations, the Company conducts the Familiarisation Program for
Independent Directors as well as other Directors on the Board about their roles, rights, responsibilities in the Company, nature of
the industry in which the Company operates, business model of the Company, etc., through various initiatives. The Company
also shares the organogram and important organisational changes on a regular basis. A few initiatives under familiarisation
program are elaborated at https://www.persistent.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Familiarization-Programme-2025-26.
pdf
Board deliberations on strategy planning
As part of our annual strategy planning process, the Company organises sessions for the Board Members and Senior Executives
to deliberate on various topics related to technological overview, global scenario for the IT industry, sales strategy, market
research, risk overview, succession planning and strategic programs required to achieve the Company’s long-term objectives.
The Company organises periodic planning meetings called the ‘Huddle’, which is attended by all the senior sales and delivery
leaders of the Organisation. Board Members participate in the Huddle to get a first-hand view of the strategy planning and
implementation process and guide the leadership by offering their expertise.
This serves a dual purpose of providing a platform for Board Members to bring their expertise to the projects, while also
providing an opportunity for them to understand detailed aspects of execution and challenges relating to the business of
the Company.
Whistleblower Policy
The Board of Directors of the Company has a Whistleblower Policy for employees and non-employee stakeholders in India and
all global locations. The employees are encouraged to report to the Whistleblower Administrator if they observe any fraudulent
financial or other information or conduct that results in instances of unethical behaviour, or actual or suspected violations of the
Company’s Code of Conduct and the Ethics Policy.
The employees are actively encouraged to reach out to the Whistleblower Administrator if they observe any fraudulent activity,
questionable financial practices, or conduct that appears unethical, or if they suspect violations of the Company’s Code of
Conduct or Ethics Policy. Beginning FY 2025-26, the Head of the Ethics Committee serves as the Whistleblower Administrator,
personally overseeing the investigation process from the initial complaint through to its resolution. All findings and outcomes
are subsequently reported to the Chairperson of the Audit Committee. Importantly, complainants are permitted to submit their
concerns in any local language, ensuring accessibility for all.
The Company has also taken proactive initiatives to train employees and raise awareness about the Vigil Mechanism, reinforcing
a culture of transparency and ethical conduct. These initiatives, along with the policy itself, provide robust safeguards to protect
employees from any form of victimisation when they report issues to the Whistleblower Administrator.

Details of Non-compliance
During the year under review, an application for compounding of an offence under Section 96 of the Companies
Act, 2013 was filed with the Regional Director, Mumbai in respect of M/s. Capiot Software Private Limited, a Wholly
Owned subsidiary Company which was merged with your Company. The said violation pertained to non-compliance
with the provisions relating to the holding of the Annual General Meeting within the prescribed timelines. The
application was duly considered by the Regional Director, Mumbai, and the offence has been compounded upon
payment of the requisite compounding fee as determined under the Act. The Company has taken note of the matter
and has instituted necessary measures to further strengthen its compliance framework and ensure adherence to
statutory timelines on a continual basis.
The aforesaid compounding does not have any material impact on the financial statements, operations, or other
business activities of the Listed Company. The management continues to maintain robust compliance systems and
periodic monitoring mechanisms to mitigate such instances going forward.
There were no non-compliances by the Company, no penalties and strictures were imposed on the Company by
Stock Exchanges, SEBI or any statutory authority, on any matter related to the capital markets, during the year
April 1, 2025, to March 31, 2026.
The Company has complied with and disclosed all the mandatory requirements under the Listing Regulations.

2. Details on Sustainable Sourcing
a. D oes the entity have procedures in place for sustainable sourcing?
Yes. Persistent Systems Limited has an end-to-end sustainable sourcing process, covering vendor screening,
contract onboarding and ongoing supplier monitoring. Sustainability considerations are embedded into
procurement through green procurement practices, assessment of environmental and social impacts prior
to contract award, and integration of environmental and social clauses in supplier contracts. Suppliers are
required to comply with the Company’s Vendor Code of Conduct, which outlines expectations on ethical
business conduct, environmental protection, labour standards, health and safety and human rights. Persistent
encourages suppliers to adopt responsible sourcing, waste reduction and energy-efficient operational
practices.
In addition, Persistent undertakes regular supplier ESG engagement and assessments, including initiatives
aligned with SEBI BRSR Core requirements, to build ESG awareness and promote responsible practices across
the value chain. These assessments and capacity-building initiatives support the identification and management
of sustainability-related risks. The Company also emphasises inclusive procurement by actively engaging local
suppliers, including MSMEs, thereby supporting local economic development while strengthening supply
chain resilience.

3. Accessibility of workplaces
Are the premises / offices of the entity accessible to differently abled employees and workers, as per the
requirements of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016? If not, whether any steps are being taken by
the entity in this regard.
Yes, Persistent Systems has a strong emphasis on accessibility and inclusion, with a focus on creating enablement
friendly workplaces for persons with disabilities. The Company is committed to providing an inclusive, barrier free
work environment and endeavours to ensure that its offices and premises are accessible in line with the Rights of
Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016, and the Harmonised Guidelines issued thereunder.
Persistent offices are designed to accommodate the needs of persons with disabilities and include features such
as accessible parking spaces, ramps at entry points, elevators, appropriate signage, disabled friendly restrooms,
and height adjustable workstations, including provisions to support wheelchair users. Across all leased facilities,
the Company ensures that accessibility requirements for persons with disabilities are duly addressed. In the digital
environment, Persistent follows recognised accessibility standards and adheres to the Web Content Accessibility
Guidelines (WCAG 2.0) to enhance accessibility of internal digital platforms. Where required, assistive
technologies and reasonable accommodations are provided to support employees with specific needs. The
Company conducts periodic reviews and audits of its facilities and undertakes necessary infrastructure upgrades
on a continuous basis to further strengthen accessibility and inclusion, ensuring that individuals of all abilities can
seamlessly access and engage with both physical and digital work environments. All our India Owned facilities
including leased facilities are accessible to Persons with Disabilities.

b. What are the processes used to identify work-related hazards and assess risks on a routine and non-routine
basis by the entity?
Persistent’s Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) programmes are designed to proactively identify, assess
and mitigate risks that could impact employee health, safety and well-being across all locations. In line with
ISO 45001:2018 principles, the company follows a structured Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment
(HIRA) approach covering all routine and non-routine activities within office premises and other operational
environments.
As a services-led organisation, our OHS risk landscape primarily includes ergonomics-related risks, psychosocial
factors, utilities and infrastructure safety, biological hazards, unsafe conditions, employee commute safety and
others. Risks are systematically assessed using a comprehensive Risk Identification and Hazard Assessment
Matrix that evaluates hazards based on severity, likelihood and potential impact. This assessment framework
covers unsafe acts, unsafe conditions, new or changed processes, equipment upgrades and non-routine
activities.
Risk identification is undertaken by process owners in consultation with safety experts, with controls
implemented in line with the hierarchy of controls. Departments set clear EHS objectives aligned to identified
risks, supported by periodic reviews and continuous improvement. Insights from incidents, audits and
operational experience are integrated into the risk assessment process to strengthen preventive controls and
ensure regulatory compliance. This structured approach supports a safe, healthy and resilient workplace.

1. Describe the processes for identifying key stakeholder groups of the entity.
The Company follows a structured process to identify key stakeholder groups based on their relationship with the
Company and relevance to its operations and value chain. Key stakeholder groups identified include employees,
customers / partners, suppliers / vendors and business partners, investors and shareholders, government
and regulators, and local communities. Stakeholder’s identification is undertaken using an impact–influence
assessment, which considers both (a) the Company’s impact on stakeholders and (b) stakeholders’ ability to
influence business outcomes. This process is integrated with the Company’s materiality assessment and risk
management framework ensuring that stakeholder expectations and concerns are systematically evaluated and
prioritised.
As part of its governance framework, the Stakeholder’s Relationship and ESG Committee oversees stakeholder
engagement through Management. The Committee regularly engages with stakeholders via multiple channels
to assess key concerns, identify material topics, and evaluate their actual and potential impacts on the business.
Inputs from these engagements are consolidated by Management and reviewed by the Committee as part of its
ongoing oversight.
The Stakeholders’ Relationship and ESG committee twice annually reviews stakeholder engagement initiatives
at each meeting, assesses progress on material topics and refines engagement approaches to enhance
effectiveness. Outcomes of these discussions are aligned with the Company’s broader ESG commitments and
strategic priorities, ensuring transparency, ethical engagement, and sustained value creation for all stakeholders
connected to the business.

4. Do you have a focal point (Individual / Committee) responsible for addressing human rights impacts or issues
caused or contributed to by the business? (Yes / No)
Yes. Persistent Systems Limited has established a structured governance mechanism to address human rights–
related concerns, anchored through its Whistleblower and Ethics framework.
The Company’s Whistleblower Policy provides a formal and transparent mechanism for employees, contractors,
and external stakeholders to report concerns, including those related to human rights, ethics, or misconduct.
Complaints can be raised confidentially through multiple reporting channels, including a toll-free helpline (India:
1800 210 0165; USA: 1 833 605 8476) and a dedicated email ID at whistleblower@persistent.com.
The mechanism is accessible to internal and external stakeholders, including employees, customers, suppliers,
community members, NGOs, and other third-parties. All complaints are subject to independent review by a
designated Investigation Team, which conducts inquiries in line with approved investigation framework.
Investigation outcomes are reviewed by the Ethics Committee, which serves as the focal committee for oversight.
The Committee approves corrective and preventive actions and monitors their implementation to closure.
Matters, where relevant, are escalated in accordance with the Company’s governance and control processes.
Whistleblower and ethics mechanisms are actively communicated to employees through internal platforms
and made available to external stakeholders via the Company website, contractual arrangements, and direct
communications. All complaints are handled with due diligence, confidentiality and protection against retaliation,
reinforcing the Company’s commitment to ethical conduct and respect for human rights.

3. Is the premise / office of the entity accessible to differently abled visitors, as per the requirements of the Rights
of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016?
Yes, Persistent Systems has a strong emphasis on accessibility and inclusion, with a focus on creating enablement
friendly workplaces for persons with disabilities. The Company is committed to providing an inclusive, barrier free
work environment and endeavours to ensure that its offices and premises are accessible in line with the Rights of
Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016, and the Harmonised Guidelines issued thereunder.
Persistent offices are designed to accommodate the needs of persons with disabilities and include features such

and height adjustable workstations, including provisions to support wheelchair users. Across all leased facilities,
the Company ensures that accessibility requirements for persons with disabilities are duly addressed. In the digital
environment, Persistent follows recognised accessibility standards and adheres to the Web Content Accessibility
Guidelines (WCAG 2.0) to enhance accessibility of internal digital platforms. Where required, assistive
technologies and reasonable accommodations are provided to support employees with specific needs. The
Company conducts periodic reviews and audits of its facilities and undertakes necessary infrastructure upgrades
on a continuous basis to further strengthen accessibility and inclusion, ensuring that individuals of all abilities can
seamlessly access and engage with both physical and digital work environments. All our India Owned facilities
including leased facilities are accessible to Persons with Disabilities.

5. Does the entity have a business continuity and disaster management plan? Give details in 100 words / web link.
Persistent Systems operates a mature, ISO/IEC 22301:2019–aligned Business Continuity Management System
(BCMS) framework, integrated with ISO/IEC 27001 controls and embedded within Enterprise Risk Management.
The framework spans all entities—subsidiaries, locations, functions and customer accounts—and is governed
by defined roles with oversight from the Board’s Risk Management Committee and the CISO. BCM is driven
by Business Impact Analysis and risk assessments, with resilience priorities aligned to financial materiality
and contractual risk. Business Continuity Plans (BCPs) are implemented for critical services and key customer
engagements, supported by industry-leading RTOs (up to 24 hours) and RPOs (up to 15 minutes). A multi-tiered
approach, integrated with cyber resilience, crisis playbooks, and SOPs, ensures effective incident response.

to validate recovery capabilities and assure readiness. Periodic reviews and test outcomes drive continuous
improvement and sustained operational resilience.

team, executes the CAPA plan. Implementation progress is monitored, reviewed periodically and updated within
the PiQ system until completion.
Resolution confirmation and formal closure: Upon resolution, the Delivery Partner secures customer
acknowledgement of closure. The SQA team validates the effectiveness of actions taken and formally closes the
escalation in PiQ, with relevant internal stakeholders kept informed.

Management Discussion and Analysis Report
Global Business Outlook
The global economy enters Financial Year 2025-26 against a backdrop of slowing growth and renewed inflationary
pressure. These conditions are linked to last year’s trade barriers and elevated uncertainty, with ongoing conflict in
the Middle East compounding the strain. The challenges are particularly acute for emerging markets and developing
economies, which remain more vulnerable to external shocks and financial instability.
While increased defense spending in response to geopolitical tension may provide a temporary boost to economic
activity, it also intensifies inflationary pressure and strains fiscal health, raising the likelihood of social unrest in fragile
regions. The overall outlook remains clouded by substantial downside risks, including prolonged conflict, deepening
geopolitical fragmentation and the resurgence of protectionist trade policies.
In this volatile environment, organisations are under pressure to strike a careful balance between cost efficiency
and the need to build resilience, agility and progress toward climate objectives, especially as regulatory frameworks
grow more complex and unpredictable. At the same time, rapid advances in automation and artificial intelligence
are helping to reduce operational workloads, but these technologies require strong governance structures and
proactive workforce reskilling to ensure successful integration. As your Company looks to 2026 and 2027, the pace of
disruption is accelerating, with technology companies moving from experimental AI pilots to large-scale, ROI-focused
deployments that prioritise safety, security and regulatory compliance, while also laying the groundwork for the
adoption of transformative quantum technologies.
Company Outlook
Your Company is a premier global provider of digital engineering and enterprise modernisation services. With more
than 27,500 employees across 21 countries, it specialises in AI-driven solutions and software product engineering for
industries such as BFSI, Healthcare and Hi-Tech, with deep expertise in building software products from conception
to deployment. Its focus is on embedding AI-driven solutions across platforms, helping enterprises move from
technical debt to competitive differentiation through a platform mindset.
Your company’s strategic approach centers on AI readiness through modern technology and data stacks, enabling
clients to become value creators. It modernises core platforms and embeds AI across operations, aligning
modernisation with strategic priorities to accelerate product launches, improve cost-to-income ratios and build
customer trust. From product engineering to cloud and AI-powered automation, your Company drives smarter, safer
and more sustainable industrial ecosystems. Its expertise in building next-generation software products at speed, with
breakthrough operational efficiency, continues to be valued by its clients and its focus on delivering insights-driven,
omnichannel customer experiences using best-in-class technologies underpins the long-term relationships it sustains
with most of its customers.
Building the AI-led Enterprise
For most enterprises, the question is no longer whether to adopt Generative AI, but where AI creates genuine value
and where greater autonomy introduces risk. The market is shifting decisively from experimentation to disciplined,
large-scale production. Generative AI is now firmly established from pilot to deployment, toward Agentic AI woven
into core business processes. Yet realising AI’s full potential remains demanding. Integrating intelligence with
existing enterprise systems is both complex and expensive and outcomes must be governed, secure and dependable
at scale.
Your Company’s AI strategy is anchored on three reinforcing pillars, underpinned by Responsible AI. Engineering
Hyper-Productivity embeds AI across the software development lifecycle, so engineering teams deliver faster, raise
quality and do more with less. Business Hyper-Productivity applies AI to automate and optimise business process
workflows and decision-making across enterprise functions, enabling organisations to drive efficiency and faster
outcomes. Enterprise Data Readiness prepares the enterprise data foundation, with the right structure, governance
and accessibility so AI can deliver accurate, contextual and trusted outcomes at scale. Together, these pillars define
the path enterprises must take to realise the full value of AI. Success lies in the last mile, making AI-driven outcomes
repeatable, transparent and governed at scale, so that the desired business outcome is sustained and trusted across
the enterprise.

Management Discussion and Analysis
Each of these pillars is brought to life by purpose-built Persistent platforms: SASVA for Engineering Hyper-
Productivity, GenAI Hub and Agent Studio for Business Hyper-Productivity, and iAURA for Enterprise Data Readiness.
These platforms together provide enterprises with a responsible, secure path to experiment with and scale AI.
SASVA 4.0 advances enterprise AI engineering further still, enabling human teams and AI agents to collaborate
within governed boundaries to raise the quality and predictability of outcomes. Its central “Brain” combines visual
control with deterministic guardrails to produce reliable, production-ready results across the entire project lifecycle.
The Persistent GenAI Hub provides a governed environment for building and operationalising AI across multiple
large language models, with built-in evaluation, observability and cost management. iAURA 2.0 applies Agentic AI to
enterprise data management, delivering flexible, scalable integration across leading cloud and large language model
providers. Together, these platforms mark a generational shift in how enterprises build, deploy and govern AI.
The 3C Framework of Persistent AI
Underpinning these platforms and client engagements is your Company’s 3C Framework — Core, Context and
Coordination — an architecture that moves AI from fragmented pilots to integrated, enterprise-wide outcomes,
and provides a repeatable path from experimentation to production at scale.
Core establishes the governed, cloud-agnostic foundation that secures, observes and cost-controls every AI workload
from day one.
Context supplies the enterprise intelligence grounding agents in verified data, knowledge graphs, institutional
memory and domain semantics so that they speak the language of the business.
Coordination orchestrates auditable, multi-agent workflows across functions and systems of record, enabling people
and agents to collaborate at production scale with full traceability.
Each pillar reinforces the others. Together, they convert isolated experiments into outcomes the business can trust
and repeat. The foundation on which your Company is building durable, AI-led transformation for its clients.
Customer Experience Practices at Persistent
Customer experience is undergoing a fundamental transformation as artificial intelligence and intelligent systems
reshape how organisations operate. Rather than simply adding new digital channels or upgrading interfaces,
businesses are now tackling the root causes of customer dissatisfaction, such as disconnected processes and manual
handoffs between departments. In the past, even advanced technologies often left gaps that required employees to
intervene, coordinate or manually resolve issues that technology alone could not address.
The emergence of AI-driven solutions marks a significant shift. These systems are now capable of proactively
managing workflows, predicting customer needs and orchestrating complex processes without constant human
oversight. By automating decision-making and communication across departments, AI helps ensure that customers
receive seamless, consistent service, reducing friction and delay. Importantly, your Company’s approach does not
focus on technology alone; it also prepares employees for new collaborative models, equipping them with the tools
and training needed to thrive alongside intelligent systems. By aligning AI initiatives with strategic business objectives
and evolving customer expectations, your Company ensures that organisations are positioned to deliver superior
experiences and maintain a competitive edge in a rapidly changing landscape.
Opportunities and Challenges
In 2026-27, the technology sector is experiencing a pivotal shift from exploratory innovation to mature, operational
execution at scale. Artificial intelligence is no longer an industry buzzword; it is now the foundation of enterprise
architecture, driving both strategy and daily operations. Companies that thrive in this environment will be those able
to demonstrate clear AI return on investment, effectively manage increasingly complex ecosystems and respond with
agility to the ongoing fragmentation of global markets and regulations.
For your Company, these changes present significant opportunities. They offer a chance to differentiate through
smarter, more responsive products and services, and a path forward in developing agentic interoperability that
enables its AI-powered systems to collaborate seamlessly across diverse cloud platforms and software ecosystems.
As quantum computing begins to deliver practical applications and AI-native development platforms transform how
teams build software, your Company’s ability to innovate swiftly and efficiently will be critical.

The Company minimises the foreign currency fluctuation risk as per the Company’s Foreign Exchange Risk
Management Policy. The Company holds plain vanilla forward contracts against a portion of expected future
receivables in USD to manage the risk of changes in exchange rates.
As per the accounting principles laid down in Ind AS 109 – ‘Financial Instruments’ relating to cash flow hedges,
derivative financial instruments which qualify for cash flow hedge accounting are fair valued at balance sheet
date and the effective portion of the resultant loss / (gain) is debited / (credited) to the hedge reserve under other
comprehensive income and
the ineffective portion is recognised in the statement of profit and loss. Derivative financial instruments are carried
as forward contract receivable when the fair value is positive and as forward contract payable when the fair value is
negative.
Changes in the fair value of derivative instruments that do not qualify for hedge accounting are recognised in the
statement of profit and loss as they arise. Hedge accounting is discontinued when the hedging instrument expires
or is sold, or terminated, or exercised or no longer qualifies for hedge accounting. Any cumulative gain or loss on the
hedging instrument recognised under other comprehensive income is transferred to the statement of profit and loss
when the forecasted transaction occurs or affects profit or loss or when a hedged transaction is no longer expected to
occur.
Accordingly, the Forward Cover Reserve (net of tax effects) as at March 31, 2026, stood at a debit balance of INR
1,676.01 Million as against a debit balance of INR 2.32 Million as at March 31, 2025. Please refer to ‘Other Equity’
under Statement of Changes in Equity in the consolidated financials for details.

Report on Risk Management
Report on Risk Management
Persistent’s Approach to Risk Management
Persistent has a robust Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) framework comprising a formal risk management policy,
defined processes, governance mechanisms, and ongoing awareness programmes. Our ERM function is focused on
strengthening and embedding a proactive risk management culture across the organisation.
The ERM function works closely with various organisational units and business leadership to facilitate the identification,
assessment, and management of risks. Oversight is provided by the Risk Management Committee (RMC) of the Board
of Directors, which was constituted on April 24, 2017, ahead of the regulatory requirement for such a committee.
ERM Objectives
The key objectives of Persistent’s ERM function are to:
• Promote an effective system to manage risks essential to support the Company’s growth strategy and business
objectives, while ensuring resilience despite changing business dynamic
• Improve institutional decision-making by providing senior management and the Board with timely and accurate
information, and proposing mitigation plans, enabling them to better comprehend the risks and opportunities at the
enterprise level and make informed decisions
• Ensure that the Company meets all legal, regulatory, and policy compliance obligations
• Establish a structured process to identify and assess risks that may impact the business continuity of the Company,
and define appropriate response and recovery plans
• Proactively identify potential risks and opportunities to prepare for future challenges and breakthroughs
• Strengthen the organisation’s ability to comprehend, manage, and control risk exposures, fostering a culture of
responsible risk-taking
• Integrate risk and opportunity assessment into the Company’s periodic planning procedures, such as strategic

• Promote a Risk-Intelligent Culture wherein conscious, enterprise-wide efforts are made to align the organisation’s
approach to risk, enabling consistent, risk-factored decision-making through targeted programmes such as Risk
Familiarisation Programmes for Directors and Key Managerial Personnel, and risk training across key functions
ERM Framework
The Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) framework adopted by Persistent is aligned with ISO Standard 31000:2018
Risk Management — Guidelines, COSO ERM — Integrating Strategy and Performance (2017), and applicable
regulatory requirements in India. The framework takes a holistic approach to identifying the full range of risks the
Company faces, with particular emphasis on those that are critical to strategic success. The framework provides
guidance on identifying, assessing, measuring, monitoring, and responding to risks across the enterprise in alignment
with the Company’s objectives and risk appetite. The ERM function reports enterprise-level risks to executive
leadership and the Risk Management Committee (RMC) of the Board on a timely basis as needed. A formal review is
conducted quarterly.
The Company’s risk management framework is further strengthened through the active involvement of internal auditors
and statutory auditors, who periodically review risk mitigation plans and related controls. Through their independent
assessments and audit processes, they provide oversight of the Company’s risk management practices — reinforcing
governance and supporting continuous improvement of enterprise risk management. The auditors also provide inputs
on key risk areas and emerging concerns as part of the overall risk management process.
Responsibility for managing risks is shared across the organisation to ensure an effective and consistent process
for avoiding and responding to risks in a timely manner. Dedicated leadership forums support the identification,
monitoring, and tracking of enterprise-level risks, while the Risk Management Committee (RMC) of the Board has
ultimate oversight of the Company’s risk management function.

ERM Process Flow
The risk management process followed at Persistent comprises the following key steps:
• Risk Identification: Identify plausible uncertainties and risks that may impact the achievement of functional, organisational,
and business objectives, or pose a threat to business continuity. This includes risks arising from internal operations as well as
external factors. Identified risks are categorised into financial, operational, reputational, regulatory, extended enterprise, strategic,
sustainability, talent, and technology for further assessment.
• Risk Analysis:
• E xisting and newly identified risks are analysed based on impact, likelihood, and velocity and are evaluated against
established risk criteria, including potential business and financial impact
• For each enterprise-level risk, Key Risk Indicators (KRIs) are defined and monitored against approved risk appetite and
tolerance thresholds to assess current risk health and the organisation’s readiness to manage it
• Where applicable, risks are assessed for potential financial exposure by identifying associated revenue, cost, or
operational drivers. Probability of occurrence, inferred from KRI performance and risk assessment, is applied to
estimate realistic downside impact and support prioritisation
• Selected risks are further analysed through scenario based assessments to evaluate the impact of plausible future
conditions such as regulatory changes, market movements, or technological developments. Scenario outcomes help
identify vulnerabilities and interdependencies, and inform mitigation planning
• Risk Prioritisation: Risks are prioritised based on criticality, emerging trends, and alignment with the Company’s objectives,
enabling focused management attention on key risks
• Risk Response: Appropriate risk response strategies are defined to avoid, mitigate, or manage key enterprise-level risks.
Mitigation plans are aligned to identified risk drivers, control effectiveness, and defined tolerance thresholds
• Monitor and Review: Mitigation actions are integrated into day-to-day operations and monitored through defined indicators.
The overall risk environment, effectiveness of mitigation measures, and emerging signals are reviewed periodically
• Reporting: Consolidated risk insights, including risk status and key trends, are reported to executive leadership and the Risk
Management Committee (RMC) of the Board on quarterly basis to support risk-informed decision-making and oversight

Highlights of FY26
FY2026 was marked by heightened geopolitical uncertainty and continued macro-economic volatility, including
regional geopolitical developments, global trade and tariff-related uncertainty, and policy-led industry considerations.
Throughout the year, the Company closely monitored these developments and activated appropriate mitigation
measures to safeguard business continuity, workforce safety, and customer delivery. The Company’s diversified
delivery footprint, established business continuity planning, and crisis management arrangements enabled stable
operations during the period. These developments did not have a material impact on the Company’s operations,
financial performance, or delivery commitments during FY 2026. However, given the evolving nature of the external
risk environment, these areas remain under active monitoring and are supported by scenario-based contingency
planning.
Geopolitical and macro-economic developments were assessed through structured enterprise-level risk reviews and
ongoing management oversight. The Company’s service-oriented business model, geographic diversification, and
limited exposure to high-risk regions supported operational resilience. Proactive stakeholder communication and
operational flexibility further enabled continuity during the year.
Against this backdrop, the Company continued to strengthen its enterprise risk management framework with a
forward-looking focus. Increased emphasis was placed on emerging and evolving risks, including artificial intelligence-
related considerations, cyber security and data privacy, regulatory and labour-law developments, and macro-economic
uncertainty. These risks were addressed through structured assessments, enhanced control frameworks, employee
awareness initiatives, and scenario-based resilience testing to support informed decision-making.
Risk governance and crisis preparedness capabilities were further enhanced during the year. An integrated risk
intelligence platform supported consolidated risk visibility, key risk indicator monitoring, and timely escalation to
senior management and the Board Risk Committee. Ongoing regulatory monitoring, materiality reassessment, and
strengthened governance practices reinforced the Company’s ability to anticipate and respond effectively to changes
in the external risk environment.
The Company believes that the continued strengthening of risk governance, resilience, and forward-looking risk
assessment capabilities remains critical to sustaining long-term growth and maintaining stakeholder confidence.

Meaning of Internal Financial Controls with Reference to Financial Statements
A company’s internal financial controls with reference to financial statements is a process designed to provide
reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for
external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. A company’s internal financial controls
with reference to financial statements include those policies and procedures that (1) pertain to the maintenance of
records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the
company; (2) provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of
financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and that receipts and expenditures
of the company are being made only in accordance with authorisations of management and directors of the company;
and (3) provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorised acquisition, use, or
disposition of the company’s assets that could have a material effect on the financial statements.
Inherent Limitations of Internal Financial Controls with Reference to Financial Statements
Because of the inherent limitations of internal financial controls with reference to financial statements, including the
possibility of collusion or improper management override of controls, material misstatements due to error or fraud
may occur and not be detected. Also, projections of any evaluation of the internal financial controls with reference
to financial statements to future periods are subject to the risk that the internal financial controls with reference to
financial statements may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance
with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.
